Rules / Maintainability

SK7060 Review commented-out statements

A standalone comment block parses as at least two code-like C# statements with substantial code punctuation.

CategoryMaintainability
Default severityhint
ScopeSyntax
Needs a compilationno
Runs under --load=looseyes
Cached per fileyes
Fixno
Language version floor—
Since1.3

Why

Disabled statements can become stale and obscure the active implementation. This is a deliberately narrow syntax heuristic: it requests review, not deletion, because a comment may be an intentional example or a record of an experiment.

Example

Instead of:

// Start();
// Process();

Write:

// Explain why an example is retained, or remove obsolete code and rely on version history.

When it does not fire

Only standalone ordinary // groups on consecutive lines and standalone /* */ comments are examined. XML documentation, inline comments, inactive preprocessor text, strings, fenced/code-tagged examples, URLs, prose, single statements, malformed comments, incomplete parses and groups over 8192 characters or 100 line comments are excluded. A 128-opening-delimiter budget bounds parser work. The complete stripped block must parse using the file's language options and contain at least two code-like atomic statements; unsupported statement forms are skipped. No semantic binding is claimed. Unlabelled multi-statement examples can still match; add a meaningful explanation or suppress the hint. No automatic deletion is offered.

Configuration

  • dotnet_diagnostic.SK7060.severity
